Downloaded:  2026-09-10, moved here from a runtime CDN fetch (previously loaded
             directly from https://docs.opencv.org/4.9.0/opencv.js at runtime — see
             js/lazyLibs.js's loadOpenCv() for why that was changed: silent quality
             degradation on a weak/no mobile connection, broken offline support for
             Document Scanner, and an SRI gap importScripts() has no native
             mechanism to close for a cross-origin script in Web Workers).

Verified:    Downloaded fresh via `curl`, computed its SHA-384 and confirmed it
             matches byte-for-byte the SRI hash this project had already been
             pinning against the CDN copy for months
             (sha384-zJHzYPWolUG4i2tYEdlq9VcmS1lGtE2r0o3EtIM+dGvmHjm0tC/DY1V1h+qSGXj9)
             — the exact same bytes already trusted, not a different build.
License:     Apache License 2.0 (OpenCV's project-wide license since v4.5.0; this
             bundled build does not embed its own license text — see OpenCV's
             own LICENSE at https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4.9.0/LICENSE
             for the authoritative full text, not reproduced here since it wasn't
             found embedded in the distributed .js file itself to copy verbatim).

Used by:     js/scanCameraUI.js (loaded via js/lazyLibs.js's loadOpenCv(), main
             thread — one-shot post-capture quad detection) and two dedicated
             Web Workers that load this same file via importScripts():
             js/scanDetectWorker.js (live-camera ~5fps framing-guide loop) and
             js/scanWarpWorker.js (perspective-warp on crop confirm). All three
             are Document Scanner's own quad-detection/perspective-correction
             pipeline (js/scanGeometry.js's detectDocumentQuad()/warpToRect())
             — lazy-loaded, costs nothing for any other page/tool.

File:        libheif-bundle.mjs
Source:      libheif-js npm package v1.19.8 (LGPL-3.0), an Emscripten/WASM
             build of libheif — package/libheif-wasm/libheif-bundle.mjs
             from the npm tarball, copied unmodified.
Downloaded:  2026-08-14
Size:        ~1.46 MB (WASM binary embedded inline as base64)
Verified:    Confirmed via `npm view libheif-js` + tarball inspection that
             this is the pre-bundled browser ESM build (self-contained,
             no separate .wasm fetch); file starts with Emscripten
             module-loader boilerplate and ends with `export{y_ as
             default}`, matching the package's own documented usage.

Used by:     js/heicDecode.js — lazy `import()`, only loaded the first
             time a user selects a .heic/.heif file for the jpg2pdf tool.
             Decodes HEIC/HEIF to JPEG entirely client-side.

Known CVEs:  Checked 2026-09-01 against published libheif CVEs from 2026
             (32740, 32741, 32814, 62291 — heap buffer overflow / heap
             out-of-bounds write / heap-memory-into-pixels disclosure,
             affecting ranges up to "1.21.2/1.22.0/1.23.0 and earlier").
             Whether libheif-js@1.19.8's bundled libheif CORE version falls
             inside any of these ranges could NOT be conclusively confirmed
             (libheif-js doesn't document its exact wrapped libheif release
             per-npm-version) — genuine uncertainty, not "probably fine."
             Real-world exposure assessed as low-to-medium: decode runs on
             the MAIN thread (see js/heicDecode.js's own header comment for
             why), triggered by any .heic/.heif upload (common — default
             iPhone photo format); worst case for the memory-disclosure-
             class CVE is same-user/same-tab-session only (this site never
             uploads files to a server, and the WASM module is a fresh
             instance per page load). No upgrade fixes this: libheif-js
             1.19.8 is the LATEST version ever published to npm (checked
             2026-09-01, no newer release exists). A CVE-patched build would
             require compiling libheif from source to WASM directly — out
             of scope for a version bump; re-check when/if libheif-js
             publishes a newer release.

See LICENSE.txt in this directory for redistribution terms (LGPL-3.0,
full text in libheif-license/LICENSE-LGPL-3.0.txt).

Files:       qpdf/worker.js, qpdf/lib/qpdf.js, qpdf/lib/qpdf.wasm
Source:      qpdf-run npm package v0.2.1 — an Emscripten/WASM build of
             qpdf. Origin tarball (qpdf-run-0.2.1.tgz) is at the repo root;
             added in commit 7b4b09d9 ("Phase 2"). Bundled qpdf core:
             11.7.0 — confirmed via the version string embedded directly in
             qpdf.wasm (`grep -a -o "qpdf [0-9.]*" lib/qpdf.wasm`), not
             assumed from the wrapper package's own version number.
Downloaded:  See commit 7b4b09d9 (predates this SOURCE.txt file — this
             entry backfilled 2026-09-01 during a security audit; qpdf had
             no provenance record here before).
Size:        ~1.8 MB (qpdf.wasm)

Used by:     js/decryptPdf.js — spawns qpdf/worker.js, runs the single CLI
             form `qpdf --decrypt --password=<pw> in.pdf out.pdf`. Two real
             call paths: (1) js/files.js's silent owner-only decrypt
             (empty password) on every uploaded PDF, feeding Merge/Split/
             Compress/pdf2jpg/pdf2word/pdf2excel/pdf2ppt/pdf2md and the
             generic worker tools; (2) the Unlock PDF tool
             (js/processor.js's _runUnlock), passing the user-typed
             password. No other qpdf subcommand (encrypt/linearize/etc.) is
             ever invoked — Protect (encrypt) is a separate, pure-JS
             RC4/AES implementation in js/pdfEncrypt.js/js/worker.js that
             does not depend on this WASM build at runtime.

Known CVEs:  CVE-2024-24246 (heap buffer overflow → crash, CVSS 5.5
             Medium) affects qpdf up to 11.8.x, fixed in 11.9.0 — applies
             to the bundled 11.7.0. DoS-only (no code-execution or data-
             disclosure component per the CVE's own CVSS vector); real-
             world exposure further bounded here by running inside an
             isolated Worker — a crash fails one operation on one file,
             not the page or other users' sessions. No upgrade fixes this:
             qpdf-run@0.2.1 is the LATEST version ever published to npm
             (checked 2026-09-01). Every alternative pre-built qpdf-WASM
             npm package checked at the same time
             (@neslinesli93/qpdf-wasm@0.3.0, qpdf-wasm-worker@0.1.0 → its
             own dependency @jspawn/qpdf-wasm@0.0.2) bundles the SAME
             11.7.0 core, not anything newer — this isn't a "hasn't been
             checked" gap, there is currently no pre-built alternative.
             A CVE-patched build would require compiling qpdf from source
             to WASM directly (Emscripten toolchain, qpdf's own native
             build dependencies) — a separate, much larger undertaking than
             a version bump, deliberately not pursued given the low
             real-world severity above. Re-check when/if qpdf-run (or any
             equivalent package) publishes a build on qpdf >= 11.9.0.

See LICENSE.txt in this directory for redistribution terms — two licenses
apply: the qpdf-run wrapper itself is MIT, but the compiled qpdf code that
makes up the bulk of qpdf.wasm is Apache License 2.0 (confirmed via the
license text compiled directly into the binary's own `--copyright` output
strings; qpdf offers Artistic License 2.0 as an alternative at the user's
option, per that same embedded text).

Source:      pdfjs-dist npm package v4.10.38, legacy/build/pdf.min.mjs and
             legacy/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs copied as is, renamed .js (both are
             ES modules; a .js name is served as JavaScript by every server).
             A folder named for the version: a cached worker of one pdf.js can't
             meet the library of another. The 3.11 worker (pdf.worker.min.js,
             loaded by pdfWorkerShim.js) stays until the previous loader has left
